output.title: Positioning drift usually starts where your words stop matching your workflow
output.body:
Positioning drift is usually not a logo problem. It starts when the words on your website, proposal, and invoice stop matching the way you actually work.

For a small business owner, that is a workflow decision, not a branding exercise. If your site says one thing, your proposal says another, and your invoice or email signature suggests a different offer again, customers will notice the mismatch before you do.

The practical next step is simple: take your last five proposals, invoices, or customer conversations and compare them with your current website copy. Look for one clear mismatch. Maybe you mention support you do not provide. Maybe the price is described differently in two places. Maybe the scope is wider on paper than it is in practice.

If you find a mismatch, decide which side changes: the documentation or the delivery. Update the words, or stop offering what the words promise. That choice stays with the owner.

If you are thinking about automating a workflow later, fix the positioning first. Otherwise the automation just preserves the confusion in a faster form. A slightly tidier mistake is still a mistake.
